newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan public sector may buy jusen-related land - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan public sector may buy jusen-related land - MOF.

text.p: Japan's Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Thursday that it was possible that public-sector firms may purchase land related to failed housing-loan companies, or "jusen".

"I think it is very possible that the public sector may buy it," Ogawa said when asked whether the government had plans to buy collateralised land, such as that previously owned by the failed housing-loan companies.
He said that once current ownership of such collateralised land was cleared up in the process of efforts to resolve the housing-loan firms' bad loans, that the land would come up for sale.
"As a result, the government and the private sector together can help promote land liquidity by making use of jusen-related land," he said.
Ogawa also said it was not wise to immediately consider tax increases as a way to correct imbalances in the state budget when the government was trying to implement fiscal reforms.
In answer to a question regarding the break-up of telecommunications giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, Ogawa said the ministry may have to consider special tax arrangements for this.
But he added that it must be careful in considering the introduction of a system of taxing firms on a consolidated basis.
